hindi: काम आदि जिसके आरम्भ में है, ऐसा घमण्ड अपनी प्रकृतियों को कुपित करता है; बुरी नीति बाहरी प्रकृतियों को।
english: Arrogance, of which desire is the first, provokes one's own constituent elements; bad policy [provokes] the external ones.
notes: 'kopayati' is understood again with 'bāhyāḥ' (prakṛtīḥ understood). utseka: literally 'overflowing, excess' (arrogance). kāma-ādiḥ could also be read as 'desire and the rest', in apposition to utsekaḥ; the bahuvrīhi reading is taken. apanaya = bad policy as the pair of naya (glossary).
lines_deva: काम.आदिर् उत्सेकः स्वाः प्रकृतीः कोपयति, अपनयो बाह्याः
lines_iast: kāma.ādir utsekaḥ svāḥ prakṛtīḥ kopayati, apanayo bāhyāḥ

hindi: वे दोनों आसुरी वृत्ति हैं।
english: Both of these are a demonic course of conduct.
notes: 'tad ubhayam' is read as 'that pair' (arrogance and bad policy of the previous unit). vṛtti may also be 'livelihood, way of life'.

hindi: अपने लोगों का विकार कोप है।
english: Revolt (kopa) is the alteration of one's own people.
notes: vikāra is rendered literally as 'alteration' (change from the normal state); 'disaffection' would be an interpretation. kopa = revolt per glossary 8.2 (the passive of kopayati in unit 1); 'anger' is the alternative sense.

hindi: दूसरे की वृद्धि के कारणों में आपत्तिरूप अर्थ, अनर्थ और संशय होते हैं।
english: In the causes of another's growth [there are] a gain that is an adversity, a loss, and a doubt.
notes: para = 'another' (usually the enemy in this text). artha rendered 'gain' and anartha 'loss' (alternatives: benefit/harm, advantage/disadvantage); this chapter's three kinds of artha-related adversity. āpad-artha is read as a karmadhāraya 'gain that is an adversity' (confirmed by unit 5). The closing iti ends the enumeration and is not rendered.

hindi: जो अर्थ प्राप्त न होने पर शत्रु की वृद्धि करता है, प्राप्त होने पर दूसरों द्वारा वापस लेने योग्य हो जाता है, अथवा प्राप्त किए जाते समय क्षय और व्यय के परिणाम वाला हो जाता है, वह आपत्तिरूप अर्थ होता है।
english: The gain which, [when] not obtained, brings about the enemy's growth; [when] obtained, becomes [something] to be taken back by others; or, while being obtained, becomes one with loss and expenditure as its outcome - that becomes a gain that is an adversity.
notes: kṣaya-vyaya-udayaḥ is taken as a bahuvrīhi 'having loss and expenditure as its rise/outcome'; alternative: a dvandva 'loss, expenditure and income (udaya)', which would give 'involves loss, expenditure and income'. pareṣām with the gerundive: 'by others' (agent), or 'of the enemies'. pratyādeya literally 'to be taken back'.
lines_deva: यो ऽर्थः शत्रु.वृद्धिम् अप्राप्तः करोति, प्राप्तः प्रत्यादेयः परेषां भवति, प्राप्यमाणो वा क्षय.व्यय.उदयो भवति, स भवत्य् आपद्.अर्थः
lines_iast: yo 'rthaḥ śatru.vṛddhim aprāptaḥ karoti, prāptaḥ pratyādeyaḥ pareṣāṃ bhavati, prāpyamāṇo vā kṣaya.vyaya.udayo bhavati, sa bhavaty āpad.arthaḥ

hindi: जैसे: पड़ोसियों के लिए चारा बना हुआ, पड़ोसी के व्यसन से उत्पन्न लाभ; शत्रु द्वारा चाहा गया अथवा अपने स्वभाव से प्राप्त करने योग्य लाभ; पीछे से कोप या पार्ष्णिग्राह द्वारा विरोध किया गया, आगे का लाभ; मित्रों के नाश या सन्धि के उल्लंघन से मण्डल द्वारा विरुद्ध किया गया लाभ - यह आपत्तिरूप अर्थ है।
english: As: an acquisition that has become bait for the neighbours and is born of a neighbour's calamity; an acquisition sought by the enemy or obtainable through [its] own nature; an acquisition in front, opposed from behind by revolt or by the heel-seizer; an acquisition opposed by the circle through the destruction of allies or a breach of treaty - such is the gain that is an adversity.
notes: Four kinds are read: (1) bait for neighbours / born of a neighbour's calamity; (2) sought by the enemy and obtainable svabhāva-adhigamya; (3) gain in front, opposed behind; (4) opposed by the maṇḍala. The first vā could instead make (2) two alternatives ('sought by the enemy' or 'obtainable by nature'). sva-bhāva-adhigamya is obscure: literally 'to be reached through own nature/state'; sense unclear, not interpreted. āmiṣa literally 'flesh, food'; 'bait' is the usual sense. vigṛhīta = 'opposed' (literally 'seized apart; at strife with'). kopa = revolt as in unit 3; alternative 'by anger'. purastāt-lābha: purastāt 'in front'. Reviewer: the vā stands between śatru-prārthitaḥ and sva-bhāva-adhigamyaḥ, so item 2 is rendered 'sought by the enemy or obtainable through its own nature' (one acquisition with two alternative qualifiers); sense of svabhāva-adhigamya still unclear.
lines_deva: यथा सामन्तानाम् आमिष.भूतः सामन्त.व्यसनजो लाभः, शत्रु.प्रार्थितो वा स्व.भाव.अधिगम्यो लाभः, पश्चात् कोपेन पार्ष्णि.ग्राहेण वा विगृहीतः पुरस्ताल्.लाभः, मित्र.उच्छेदेन सन्धि.व्यतिक्रमेण वा मण्डल.विरुद्धो लाभः इत्य् आपद्.अर्थः
lines_iast: yathā sāmantānām āmiṣa.bhūtaḥ sāmanta.vyasanajo lābhaḥ, śatru.prārthito vā sva.bhāva.adhigamyo lābhaḥ, paścāt kopena pārṣṇi.grāheṇa vā vigṛhītaḥ purastāl.lābhaḥ, mitra.ucchedena sandhi.vyatikrameṇa vā maṇḍala.viruddho lābhaḥ ity āpad.arthaḥ

hindi: अपने से अथवा दूसरे से भय की उत्पत्ति - यह अनर्थ है।
english: The arising of fear from oneself or from another - such is a loss.
lines_deva: स्वतः परतो वा भय.उत्पत्तिर् इत्य् अनर्थः
lines_iast: svataḥ parato vā bhaya.utpattir ity anarthaḥ

hindi: उन दोनों में संशय है: “अर्थ है या नहीं?”, “अनर्थ है या नहीं?”, “अर्थ अनर्थ है?”, “अनर्थ अर्थ है?”
english: Of these two, [there is] doubt: “a gain, or not?”; “a loss, or not?”; “[is the] gain a loss?”; “[is the] loss a gain?”
notes: Four forms of doubt, each quoted with iti; the iti closing a quotation is not rendered. 'tayoḥ' = artha and anartha. The e-text prints 'tayoḥ artho' with hiatus (no sandhi).
lines_deva: तयोः अर्थो न वा-इति, अनर्थो न वा-इति, अर्थो ऽनर्थ इति, अनर्थो ऽर्थ इति संशयः
lines_iast: tayoḥ artho na vā-iti, anartho na vā-iti, artho 'nartha iti, anartho 'rtha iti saṃśayaḥ

hindi: संशय: “शत्रु के मित्र को उभारने में अर्थ है या नहीं?”
english: Doubt: “To rouse the enemy's ally - [is it] a gain, or not?”
notes: utsāhayati = rouse (glossary 13.1).
lines_deva: शत्रु.मित्रम् उत्साहयितुम् अर्थो न वा-इति संशयः
lines_iast: śatru.mitram utsāhayitum artho na vā-iti saṃśayaḥ

hindi: संशय: “शत्रु की सेना को धन और मान द्वारा बुला लाने में अनर्थ है या नहीं?”
english: Doubt: “To draw in the enemy's army by wealth and honour - [is it] a loss, or not?”
notes: artha in artha-mānābhyām is 'wealth' (the means), not the technical 'gain' of this chapter. āvāhayitum: caus. of ā-√vah 'to cause to come, bring over'; 'draw in' is literal-natural; the exact sense (summon, attract, invite) is not fixed.
lines_deva: शत्रु.बलम् अर्थ.मानाभ्याम् आवाहयितुम् अनर्थो न वा-इति संशयः
lines_iast: śatru.balam artha.mānābhyām āvāhayitum anartho na vā-iti saṃśayaḥ

hindi: संशय: “बलवान् पड़ोसियों वाली भूमि को लेने में अर्थ अनर्थ है?”
english: Doubt: “To take land having strong neighbours - [is the] gain a loss?”
lines_deva: बलवत्.सामन्तां भूमिम् आदातुम् अर्थो ऽनर्थ इति संशयः
lines_iast: balavat.sāmantāṃ bhūmim ādātum artho 'nartha iti saṃśayaḥ

hindi: संशय: “अधिक बलवान् के साथ मिलकर प्रयाण करने में अनर्थ अर्थ है?”
english: Doubt: “A joint march with a stronger one - [is the] loss a gain?”

text_flags.why: possible typo: jāyasā is not a recognisable form; the instrumental of the comparative jyāyas 'stronger' fits sambhūya-yānam 'march together with'

notes: Reading relies on the suggested jyāyasā. sambhūya-yāna literally 'going having come together'. The unit is an anartha-artha doubt (loss a gain?), the reverse of unit 11.
lines_deva: जायसा सम्भूययानम् अनर्थो ऽर्थ इति संशयः

hindi: इनमें से अर्थ के संशय की ओर जाए।
english: Of these, he should approach [the case of] doubt about gain.
notes: Obscure: upa-√gam 'approach, go to, undergo'. The sense may be 'he should embark on the cases where gain is doubtful' or 'he should resort to the doubtful-gain case'. Rendered literally; no interpretation added.

hindi: अर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अर्थ है; अर्थ, अनुबन्ध-रहित; अर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अनर्थ है; अनर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अर्थ है; अनर्थ, अनुबन्ध-रहित; अनर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अनर्थ है - यह अनुबन्ध का छह-वर्ग है।
english: A gain with gain as its sequel; a gain without sequel; a gain with loss as its sequel; a loss with gain as its sequel; a loss without sequel; a loss with loss as its sequel - such is the sixfold group of sequels.
notes: anubandha = 'sequel, consequence' (literally 'binding on'). ṣaṭ-varga restored from the printed ṣaḍ.
lines_deva: अर्थो ऽर्थ.अनुबन्धः, अर्थो निरनुबन्धः, अर्थो ऽनर्थ.अनुबन्धः, अनर्थो ऽर्थ.अनुबन्धः, अनर्थो निरनुबन्धः, अनर्थो ऽनर्थ.अनुबन्धः इत्य् अनुबन्ध.षड्.वर्गः
lines_iast: artho 'rtha.anubandhaḥ, artho niranubandhaḥ, artho 'nartha.anubandhaḥ, anartho 'rtha.anubandhaḥ, anartho niranubandhaḥ, anartho 'nartha.anubandhaḥ ity anubandha.ṣaḍ.vargaḥ

hindi: शत्रु को उखाड़कर पार्ष्णिग्राह द्वारा ग्रहण - अर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अनर्थ है।
english: Having uprooted an enemy, the taking by the heel-seizer - a gain with loss as its sequel.
notes: pārṣṇi-grāha-ādāna is obscure: 'taking (of it) by the heel-seizer' (genitive/agent reading) or 'taking up/seizing the heel-seizer'. The first is used. What the heel-seizer takes (the enemy's land or the gain) is not stated.

hindi: उदासीन पर सेना से अनुग्रह, फल द्वारा - अर्थ, अनुबन्ध-रहित।
english: Favouring the neutral king with the army, by the result - a gain without sequel.
notes: Obscure: daṇḍa-anugraha may be 'favour (shown) with the army' to the neutral king, or 'favour of the army (to him)'; 'phalena' (by the result / with the fruit) may mean 'in return for a reward' or 'by what it yields'. Rendered literally. The e-text prints 'phalena artho' with hiatus.

hindi: दूसरे का भीतर से उन्मूलन - अर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अनर्थ है।
english: The uprooting from within of another - a gain with loss as its sequel.
notes: antar-ucchedana: antar 'within' + ucchedana 'uprooting'; the sense (destroying from inside, or destroying the inner part of the other) is not certain. para = 'another' (probably the enemy).

hindi: शत्रु के पड़ोसी पर कोश और दण्ड से अनुग्रह - अनर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अनर्थ है।
english: Favour to the enemy's neighbour with treasury and army - a loss with loss as its sequel.
notes: prativeśa literally 'neighbour (of the next house)'. daṇḍa = army as a constituent element (glossary).

hindi: कम शक्ति वाले को उभारकर निवृत्ति - अनर्थ, अनुबन्ध-रहित।
english: Having roused one of weak power, withdrawal - a loss without sequel.
notes: nivṛtti literally 'turning back, ceasing'; whose withdrawal (the rouser's) is not stated.

hindi: अधिक बलवान् को उठाकर निवृत्ति - अनर्थ, जिसका अनुबन्ध अनर्थ है।
english: Having stirred up a stronger one, withdrawal - a loss with loss as its sequel.
notes: utthāpya (caus. 'having made rise') rendered 'stirred up'. jyāyas 'greater, stronger'.

hindi: इनमें पहले-पहले वाला प्राप्त करने के लिए अधिक श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Of these, each earlier one is better to encounter.
notes: 'each' renders the repetition pūrvaḥ pūrvaḥ (distributive). The six kinds of unit 14 are meant (in the order listed).

words.gloss: setting in order of the undertakings

hindi: यह कार्यों की अवस्थापना है।
english: Such is the setting in order of the undertakings.
notes: kārya 'what is to be done' (undertaking, matter, case); avasthāpana 'placing in position, arrangement'.

hindi: चारों ओर से एक साथ अर्थ की उत्पत्ति चारों ओर से अर्थ की आपत्ति होती है।
english: The simultaneous arising of gain from all sides is, from all sides, an adversity of gain.
notes: artha-āpad is read 'adversity of gain' (the situation of unit 4 and 5, 'āpad-artha').

hindi: वही पार्ष्णिग्राह द्वारा विरोध की गई होने पर चारों ओर से अर्थ के संशय की आपत्ति हो जाती है।
english: That same [adversity], opposed by the heel-seizer, becomes from all sides an adversity of doubt about gain.
notes: 'sā' (f.) refers back to the feminine arising/adversity of unit 23; supplied in brackets in English.

words.gloss: from the support of the ally and the rear ally

hindi: उन दोनों में मित्र और आक्रन्द के उपग्रह से सिद्धि होती है।
english: In those two, success [comes] from the support of the ally and the rear ally.
notes: upagraha: 'support, securing, taking in hand'; the genitive may be subjective (the ally's support) or objective (supporting the ally); left open as in English 'support'. 'tayoḥ' = the two adversities of units 23 and 24. ākranda = rear ally (glossary).

hindi: चारों ओर से शत्रुओं से भय की उत्पत्ति चारों ओर से अनर्थ की आपत्ति होती है।
english: From all sides, the arising of fear from enemies is, from all sides, an adversity of loss.

text_flags.why: typo (doubled t): samantataḥ + 'nartha gives samantato 'nartha, as in the parallel lines 23 and 27

lines_deva: समन्ततः शत्रुभ्यो भय.उत्पत्तिः समन्त्तो ऽनर्थ.आपद् भवति

hindi: वही मित्र द्वारा विरोध की गई होने पर चारों ओर से अनर्थ के संशय की आपत्ति हो जाती है।
english: That same [adversity], opposed by an ally, becomes from all sides an adversity of doubt about loss.

words.gloss: from the support of the unsteady enemy and the rear ally
non-remedy of what is mixed with the other

hindi: उन दोनों में चंचल शत्रु और आक्रन्द के उपग्रह से सिद्धि होती है, अथवा दूसरे से मिले हुए का प्रतिकार न करना।
english: In those two, success [comes] from the support of the unsteady enemy and the rear ally, or non-remedy of [what is] mixed with the other.

text_flags.why: possible: miśra here is obscure; 'mitra' (an enemy's ally) would fit the chapter context (cf. unit 9 śatru-mitra), but the printed text is kept

notes: Obscure and uncertain: 'para-miśra' is rendered literally ('other' + 'mixed'); no sense has been decided. cala-amitra-ākranda: 'cala' (unsteady, wavering) may qualify only amitra or the whole pair; the pair 'enemy and rear ally' is the reading used. sandhi: printed tayoś before c. Reviewer: the para-mitra flag is only a conjecture; 9.6 has para-miśrā as a technical name (glossary 9.6), so para-miśra may well be the genuine reading. Printed text kept; a person should check against Kangle's apparatus.

hindi: “इधर से लाभ, उधर से लाभ”: दोनों ओर से अर्थ की आपत्ति होती है।
english: “Acquisition from this side, acquisition from the other side”: from both sides there is an adversity of gain.
lines_deva: इतो लाभ इतरतो लाभ इत्य् उभयतो ऽर्थ.आपद् भवति
lines_iast: ito lābha itarato lābha ity ubhayato 'rtha.āpad bhavati

words.gloss: endowed with the quality of acquisition

hindi: और चारों ओर से अर्थ वाली उस आपत्ति में लाभ-गुण से युक्त अर्थ को लेने के लिए प्रयाण करे।
english: And in that [adversity] with gain on all sides, he should march to take the gain endowed with the quality of acquisition.
notes: Token order is tasyām, samantato 'rthāyām, ca; āpad (f.) is understood. lābha-guṇa = the advantage or quality of the acquisition (not further defined here). The ca could also join tasyām with the second locative: 'in that, and in the one with gain on all sides'.
lines_deva: तस्यां समन्ततो ऽर्थायां च लाभ.गुण.युक्तम् अर्थम् आदातुं यायात्
lines_iast: tasyāṃ samantato 'rthāyāṃ ca lābha.guṇa.yuktam artham ādātuṃ yāyāt

hindi: लाभ-गुण के समान होने पर, प्रधान को, निकटवर्ती को, न छूटने वाले को, अथवा जिससे वह न्यून हो - उसे लेने के लिए प्रयाण करे।
english: When the quality of acquisition is equal, he should march to take that - the chief, the near, the not slipping away [gain], or [the one] by which he would be deficient.
notes: The accusative adjectives agree with the understood artham of unit 30. anatipātin: 'not passing by / not slipping away'; sense uncertain. 'ūno vā yena bhavet' literally 'or by which he would be deficient'; the exact sense (the one whose lack leaves him deficient) is not decided. 'tam' resumes the whole list.
lines_deva: तुल्ये लाभ.गुणे प्रधानम् आसन्नम् अनतिपातिनम् ऊनो वा येन भवेत् तम् आदातुं यायात्
lines_iast: tulye lābha.guṇe pradhānam āsannam anatipātinam ūno vā yena bhavet tam ādātuṃ yāyāt

hindi: “इधर से अनर्थ, उधर से अनर्थ”: दोनों ओर से अनर्थ की आपत्ति है।
english: “Loss from this side, loss from the other side”: from both sides there is an adversity of loss.
lines_deva: इतो ऽनर्थ इतरतो ऽनर्थ इत्य् उभयतो ऽनर्थ.आपत्

hindi: और चारों ओर से अनर्थ वाली उस आपत्ति में मित्रों से सिद्धि पाने की इच्छा करे।
english: And in that [adversity] with loss on all sides, he should seek to obtain success from allies.
notes: āpad (f.) understood, as in unit 30.
lines_deva: तस्यां समन्ततो ऽनर्थायां च मित्रेभ्यः सिद्धिं लिप्सेत
lines_iast: tasyāṃ samantato 'narthāyāṃ ca mitrebhyaḥ siddhiṃ lipseta

words.gloss: in the absence of an ally

hindi: मित्र के अभाव में, प्रकृतियों में से अपेक्षाकृत छोटी प्रकृति से एक ओर से अनर्थ वाली आपत्ति को साधे, अधिक बड़ी प्रकृति से दोनों ओर से अनर्थ वाली को, और मूल से चारों ओर से अनर्थ वाली का प्रतिकार करे।
english: In the absence of an ally, he should overcome [the adversity] with loss on one side by the lesser of the constituent elements, [that] with loss on both sides by the greater, [and that] with loss on all sides he should remedy by the root.

text_flags.why: possible: an instrumental feminine laghīyasyā is expected (parallel to jyāyasyā); the print reads laghīyasyaikato where ā + e gives ai, so the e-text's unsandhied join may have shortened the vowel

notes: āpad (f.) understood with the three accusative feminines. sādh (caus.) rendered 'overcome' (also 'accomplish, subdue, settle'); sense uncertain. prakṛti = constituent element (glossary). mūla literally 'root' (here the most basic of the elements; not specified). The 'lesser/greater' prakṛti is not specified.
lines_deva: मित्र.अभावे प्रकृतीनां लघीयस्य-एकतो ऽनर्थां साधयेत्, उभयतो ऽनर्थां ज्यायस्या, समन्ततो ऽनर्थां मूलेन प्रतिकुर्यात्
lines_iast: mitra.abhāve prakṛtīnāṃ laghīyasya-ekato 'narthāṃ sādhayet, ubhayato 'narthāṃ jyāyasyā, samantato 'narthāṃ mūlena pratikuryāt

hindi: असम्भव होने पर सब कुछ छोड़कर चला जाए।
english: When [this is] impossible, having abandoned everything, he should go away.

hindi: क्योंकि जीवित रहने वाले का फिर लौटना देखा गया है, जैसे सुयात्र और उदयन का।
english: For the coming back again of one who lives is seen, as with Suyatra and Udayana.
notes: Suyatra and Udayana: names (persons), not further identified; the first name's stem (suyātra or suyātrā) is uncertain from the e-text; the English form follows the glossary (no diacritics). The instrumental dual is rendered 'as with'.
lines_deva: दृष्टा हि जीवतः पुनर्.आवृत्तिर् यथा सुयात्रा.उदयनाभ्याम्
lines_iast: dṛṣṭā hi jīvataḥ punar.āvṛttir yathā suyātrā.udayanābhyām

hindi: “इधर से लाभ, उधर से राज्य पर आक्रमण”: दोनों ओर से अर्थ और अनर्थ की आपत्ति होती है।
english: “Acquisition from this side, assault on the kingdom from the other side”: from both sides there is an adversity of gain and loss.
notes: abhimarśa literally 'touching, handling'; 'assault' is the usual sense in this context.
lines_deva: इतो लाभ इतरतो राज्य.अभिमर्श इत्य् उभयतो ऽर्थ.अनर्थ.आपद् भवति
lines_iast: ito lābha itarato rājya.abhimarśa ity ubhayato 'rtha.anartha.āpad bhavati

hindi: उस आपत्ति में जो अर्थ अनर्थ को साधने वाला हो, उसे लेने के लिए प्रयाण करे।
english: In that [adversity], he should march to take the gain which overcomes the loss.
notes: sādhaka (agent of √sādh) rendered 'that overcomes' as in sādhayet (units 34, 42); literal alternative 'accomplishing'. The sense is uncertain.
lines_deva: तस्याम् अनर्थ.साधको यो ऽर्थस् तम् आदातुं यायात्
lines_iast: tasyām anartha.sādhako yo 'rthas tam ādātuṃ yāyāt

hindi: अन्यथा तो राज्य पर आक्रमण को रोके।
english: Otherwise, indeed, he should ward off the assault on the kingdom.

hindi: इससे चारों ओर से अर्थ और अनर्थ की आपत्ति की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this, the adversity of gain and loss from all sides is explained.

words.gloss: of loss and doubt about gain

hindi: “इधर से अनर्थ, उधर से अर्थ का संशय”: दोनों ओर से अनर्थ और अर्थ के संशय वाली।
english: “Loss from this side, doubt about gain from the other side”: [the adversity is] one of loss and of doubt about gain from both sides.
notes: The last word is a feminine adjective; āpad (f.) and the verb are not stated (supplied in brackets in English). The compound is parsed as anartha + artha-saṃśaya; it could instead read 'doubt about loss and gain'. Reviewer: 'saṃśayā' is probably a truncation of saṃśaya-āpad (cf. units 24, 37): the e-text may have dropped -pad. Draft's feminine-adjective reading is a fallback only; text_flag suggested but not addable by patch.
lines_deva: इतो ऽनर्थ इतरतो ऽर्थ.संशय इत्य् उभयतो ऽनर्थ.अर्थ.संशया

hindi: उस आपत्ति में पहले अनर्थ को साधे, उसके सिद्ध होने पर अर्थ के संशय को।
english: In that [adversity], he should first overcome the loss; on that being accomplished, [he should overcome] the doubt about gain.
notes: The verb sādhayet is understood with artha-saṃśayam; sādh rendered 'overcome' as in unit 34 (sense uncertain).
lines_deva: तस्यां पूर्वम् अनर्थं साधयेत्, तत्.सिद्धाव् अर्थ.संशयम्
lines_iast: tasyāṃ pūrvam anarthaṃ sādhayet, tat.siddhāv artha.saṃśayam

hindi: इससे सब ओर अनर्थ और अर्थ के संशय की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this, [the adversity of] doubt of loss and gain on all sides is explained.
notes: The feminine nom. sg. saṃśayā/vyākhyātā agrees with an understood āpad (adversity), as in unit 44; the supplied noun is bracketed in English only.

words.gloss: adversity of doubt of gain and loss

hindi: “इधर अर्थ, उधर अनर्थ का संशय” — दोनों ओर अर्थ और अनर्थ के संशय की आपत्ति।
english: “Gain on this side, doubt of loss on the other” — the adversity of doubt of gain and loss on both sides.
lines_deva: इतो ऽर्थ इतरतो ऽनर्थ.संशय इत्य् उभयतो ऽर्थ.अनर्थ.संशय.आपद्

hindi: इससे सब ओर अर्थ और अनर्थ के संशय की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this, [the adversity of] doubt of gain and loss on all sides is explained.
notes: Same construction as unit 43; the feminine agreement points to an understood āpad.

hindi: उसमें प्रकृतियों में से हर पहली को अनर्थ के संशयों से छुड़ाने का प्रयत्न करे।
english: In that, one should strive to free each earlier one of the constituent elements from doubts of loss.
notes: The grammar is loose: pūrvāṃ pūrvām (f. acc. sg.) with anartha-saṃśayān (m. acc. pl.) both as accusatives. Alternative: pūrvān pūrvān (m. acc. pl.) agreeing with saṃśayān, i.e. "the earlier and earlier doubts of loss of the constituent elements". Draft keeps the printed reading.
lines_deva: तस्यां पूर्वां पूर्वां प्रकृतीनाम् अनर्थ.संशयान् मोक्षयितुं यतेत
lines_iast: tasyāṃ pūrvāṃ pūrvāṃ prakṛtīnām anartha.saṃśayān mokṣayituṃ yateta

hindi: क्योंकि अनर्थ के संशय में खड़ा मित्र अधिक अच्छा है, दण्ड नहीं; अथवा दण्ड, कोश नहीं।
english: For better is the ally standing in doubt of loss, not the army; or the army, not the treasury.
notes: tiṣṭhan is masculine while mitram is neuter; the agreement is loose (an understood person or the king standing in doubt is possible). Closing iti not rendered. Order of exposure: ally, then army, then treasury.
lines_deva: श्रेयो हि मित्रम् अनर्थ.संशये तिष्ठन् न दण्डः, दण्डो वा न कोश इति
lines_iast: śreyo hi mitram anartha.saṃśaye tiṣṭhan na daṇḍaḥ, daṇḍo vā na kośa iti

words.gloss: in the absence of complete freeing

hindi: सम्पूर्ण छुड़ाने के अभाव में प्रकृतियों के अंशों को छुड़ाने का प्रयत्न करे।
english: In the absence of complete freeing, one should strive to free parts of the constituent elements.

words.gloss: excluding the fierce and the greedy

hindi: वहाँ मनुष्य-प्रकृतियों में बहुत या अनुरक्त को, तीक्ष्ण और लोभी को छोड़कर; द्रव्य-प्रकृतियों में बहुमूल्य या बड़े उपकार वाले को।
english: There, of the human constituent elements, [one should free] the large or the devoted [part], excluding the fierce and the greedy; of the material constituent elements, the valuable [part] or that of great usefulness.
notes: Verb and noun "part" supplied from unit 48 (bracketed in English). tīkṣṇa rendered literally as "fierce"; the glossary sense "assassin" belongs to the agent contexts and is only an alternative here. bahulam could be "numerous" or "large"; the word supplied after anuraktam is uncertain. Review: tīkṣṇa kept 'fierce' (adjective of persons beside lubdha), as in 9.6 where the target is 'fierce'; 'assassin' only for the agent class.
lines_deva: तत्र पुरुष.प्रकृतीनां बहुलम् अनुरक्तं वा तीक्ष्ण.लुब्ध.वर्जम्, द्रव्य.प्रकृतीनां सारं महा.उपकारं वा
lines_iast: tatra puruṣa.prakṛtīnāṃ bahulam anuraktaṃ vā tīkṣṇa.lubdha.varjam, dravya.prakṛtīnāṃ sāraṃ mahā.upakāraṃ vā

hindi: हल्के सन्धि, आसन अथवा द्वैधीभाव से, भारी विपरीतों से।
english: The light ones: by peace, staying quiet (āsana) or the dual policy; the heavy ones: by the opposites.
notes: No verb in the Sanskrit; the neuter plurals laghūni/gurūṇi have no stated noun (the adversities or doubts of the preceding passage are probable). āsana literally "sitting". viparyayaiḥ: by the contrary [means]. Review: sandhi = peace (as 8.5, 12.5); āsana = staying quiet; dvaidhī-bhāva = the dual policy. laghūni/gurūṇi left without a stated noun.
lines_deva: सन्धिना-आसनेन द्वैधी.भावेन वा लघूनि, विपर्ययैर् गुरूणि
lines_iast: sandhinā-āsanena dvaidhī.bhāvena vā laghūni, viparyayair gurūṇi

hindi: और क्षय, स्थान और वृद्धि में से उत्तरोत्तर को प्राप्त करना चाहे।
english: And of decline, stagnation and growth, one should seek to obtain the later and later one.

hindi: अथवा उलटे क्रम से क्षय आदि के भविष्य में विशेष को देखे।
english: Or, by the reverse order, one should see the difference of decline and the rest in the future.
notes: viśeṣa is "difference" or "distinction"; "advantage" is a possible alternative sense. prātilomya = reversal of the order of unit 51. Review: viśeṣa kept literal ('difference'); the whole is obscure (choosing among decline, stagnation, growth by the later outcome).
lines_deva: प्रातिलोम्येन वा क्षय.आदीनाम् आयत्यां विशेषं पश्येत्
lines_iast: prātilomyena vā kṣaya.ādīnām āyatyāṃ viśeṣaṃ paśyet

hindi: इस प्रकार देश का निर्धारण।
english: Thus, the determination of place.

words.gloss: at the beginning, middle and end of the march

hindi: इससे यात्रा के आदि, मध्य और अन्त में अर्थ, अनर्थ और संशयों की प्राप्ति की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this, the encountering of gain, loss and doubt at the beginning, middle and end of the march is explained.
notes: Compound artha-anartha-saṃśayānām read as three items (gain, loss, doubt) because of the plural saṃśayānām; "doubt of gain and loss" is the alternative. upasamprāpti rendered "encountering"; "attainment" is possible. Review: upasamprāpti = encountering (glossary 9.7); three items read, as in 55 and 57.

words.gloss: at the start of the march
in the warding off of the heel-seizer and the reinforcer
in decline, expenditure, absence abroad and recovery
in the protections of the root

hindi: और अर्थ, अनर्थ और संशयों का निरन्तर सम्बन्ध होने से यात्रा के आरम्भ में अर्थ प्राप्त करना अधिक अच्छा है, और पार्ष्णिग्राह तथा आसार के निवारण में, क्षय, व्यय, प्रवास और पुनः ग्रहण में तथा मूल की रक्षाओं में होता है।
english: And because of the continuous connection of gain, loss and doubt, gain is better to encounter at the start of the march, and it is [so] in warding off the heel-seizer and the reinforcer, in decline, expenditure, absence abroad and recovery, and in the protections of the root.
notes: The syntax of the closing series is loose: "bhavati" is taken as "is [so]" for the series pārṣṇi-grāha-āsāra-pratighāte ... mūla-rakṣaṇeṣu. pratyādeya = "to be taken back / recovery" is uncertain (alternative: restoration of what was taken). pravāsa = living away from home. mūla = root or base (the home territory). The Hindi attaches "ca ... bhavati" at the end.
lines_deva: निरन्तर.योगित्वाच् च-अर्थ.अनर्थ.संशयानां यात्रा.आदाव् अर्थः श्रेयान् उपसम्प्राप्तुं पार्ष्णि.ग्राह.आसार.प्रतिघाते क्षय.व्यय.प्रवास.प्रत्यादेये मूल.रक्षणेषु च भवति
lines_iast: nirantara.yogitvāc ca-artha.anartha.saṃśayānāṃ yātrā.ādāv arthaḥ śreyān upasamprāptuṃ pārṣṇi.grāha.āsāra.pratighāte kṣaya.vyaya.pravāsa.pratyādeye mūla.rakṣaṇeṣu ca bhavati

words.gloss: of one standing on his own ground

hindi: वैसे ही अपनी भूमि पर खड़े रहने वाले के लिए अनर्थ या संशय सहने योग्य होता है।
english: Likewise, loss or doubt is bearable for one standing on his own ground.
lines_deva: तथा-अनर्थः संशयो वा स्व.भूमिष्ठस्य विषह्यो भवति
lines_iast: tathā-anarthaḥ saṃśayo vā sva.bhūmiṣṭhasya viṣahyo bhavati

words.gloss: in the middle of the march

hindi: इससे यात्रा के मध्य में अर्थ, अनर्थ और संशयों की प्राप्ति की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this, the encountering of gain, loss and doubt in the middle of the march is explained.

words.gloss: at the end of the march
from fear of harassment by the enemy

hindi: किन्तु यात्रा के अन्त में, क्षीण करने योग्य अथवा उच्छेद करने योग्य को क्षीण करके या उखाड़कर, अर्थ प्राप्त करना अधिक अच्छा है, अनर्थ या संशय नहीं, शत्रु की बाधा के भय से।
english: But at the end of the march, gain is better to encounter, after weakening or uprooting [the one] to be weakened or to be uprooted, not loss or doubt, from fear of harassment by the enemy.
notes: The objects of karśayitvā/ucchidya are taken to be the two gerundives (an understood enemy). para = "the other", rendered "the enemy"; ābādha = harassment or trouble.
lines_deva: यात्रा.अन्ते तु कर्शनीयम् उच्छेदनीयं वा कर्शयित्वा-उच्छिद्य वा-अर्थः श्रेयान् उपसम्प्राप्तुं न-अनर्थः संशयो वा पर.आबाध.भयात्
lines_iast: yātrā.ante tu karśanīyam ucchedanīyaṃ vā karśayitvā-ucchidya vā-arthaḥ śreyān upasamprāptuṃ na-anarthaḥ saṃśayo vā para.ābādha.bhayāt

words.gloss: of one who is not the leader
reaching the middle or end of the march

hindi: किन्तु सामवायिकों में जो अग्रणी नहीं है, उसके लिए यात्रा के मध्य या अन्त तक पहुँचने वाला अनर्थ या संशय प्राप्त करना अधिक अच्छा है, बिना आग्रह के चलने के कारण।
english: But for one who is not the leader of the associates, loss or doubt reaching the middle or end of the march is better to encounter, because of going without insistence.
notes: Obscure: sāmavāyika (associates, members of a joint undertaking), apuroga (not going in front), -ga ("going to" or "occurring in") and anirbandha-gāmitva (going without insistence or stubbornness) are rendered literally. Who goes without insistence (the associates or the follower) is not stated. Alternative: "occurring in the middle or at the end of the march". Review: the two genitives sāmavāyikānām apurogasya may also be read separately; Hindi 'सामवायिकों में' is loose for a genitive. Low confidence kept; sense of -ga and anirbandha unresolved.
lines_deva: सामवायिकानाम् अपुरोगस्य तु यात्रा.मध्य.अन्तगो ऽनर्थः संशयो वा श्रेयान् उपसम्प्राप्तुम् अनिर्बन्ध.गामित्वात्
lines_iast: sāmavāyikānām apurogasya tu yātrā.madhya.antago 'narthaḥ saṃśayo vā śreyān upasamprāptum anirbandha.gāmitvāt

hindi: “अर्थ, धर्म, काम” — अर्थ का त्रिवर्ग है।
english: “Gain, dharma, desire” — the triad of gain.
notes: artha-tri-varga: the triad headed by artha (the group of three whose first member is gain); iti shown by the quotation marks.

hindi: उसमें पहले-पहले को प्राप्त करना अधिक अच्छा है।
english: Of that, each earlier one is better to encounter.

hindi: “अनर्थ, अधर्म, शोक” — अनर्थ का त्रिवर्ग है।
english: “Loss, unrighteousness, grief” — the triad of loss.

hindi: उसमें पहले-पहले का प्रतिकार करना अधिक अच्छा है।
english: Of that, each earlier one is better to remedy.

hindi: “अर्थ-अनर्थ”, “धर्म-अधर्म”, “काम-शोक” — संशय का त्रिवर्ग है।
english: “Gain [or] loss,” “dharma [or] unrighteousness,” “desire [or] grief” — the triad of doubt.
notes: The pairs are read as the doubts "is it gain or loss?" etc.; "or" is bracketed in English and shown by hyphens in Hindi. Alternative: "gain as loss" (the one taken for the other).
lines_deva: अर्थो ऽनर्थ इति, धर्मो ऽधर्म इति, कामः शोक इति संशय.त्रि.वर्गः
lines_iast: artho 'nartha iti, dharmo 'dharma iti, kāmaḥ śoka iti saṃśaya.tri.vargaḥ

words.gloss: in the success of the latter side

hindi: उसमें उत्तर पक्ष की सिद्धि होने पर पूर्व पक्ष प्राप्त करना अधिक अच्छा है।
english: Of that, in the success of the latter side, the former side is better to encounter.
notes: Obscure. tasya-uttara-pakṣa-siddhau: "of that, in the success of the latter side". Sides read as the two halves of each doubt pair of unit 64 (gain/loss etc.). siddhi could be "accomplishment, coming about"; alternative: "if the latter side is established (as certain)". Review: uttara-pakṣa/pūrva-pakṣa here = latter/former side (alternative) of a doubt pair, not the 15.1 technical 'reply/objection'. Low confidence kept.

hindi: इस प्रकार काल का निर्धारण।
english: Thus, the determination of time.

hindi: इस प्रकार आपत्तियाँ। उनकी सिद्धि।
english: Thus the adversities. Their success.
notes: GROUPING: "ity āpadaḥ" closes the preceding section on adversities, while "tāsāṃ siddhiḥ" is the heading of the next section (success against the adversities, units 68 onwards). The dash joins two separate items.

words.gloss: among townsmen, country people and chiefs of the army
among neighbouring chiefs and forest chiefs

hindi: पुत्रों, भाइयों और बन्धुओं में साम और दान से सिद्धि उचित है; नगरवासियों, जनपदवासियों और सेना के मुखियों में दान और भेद से; सामन्तों और आटविकों में भेद और दण्ड से।
english: Among sons, brothers and kinsmen, success by conciliation and gifts is suitable; among townsmen, country people and chiefs of the army, by gifts and dissension; among neighbouring chiefs and forest chiefs, by dissension and force.
notes: daṇḍa-mukhya read as "chiefs of the army" (alternative: paura-jānapada-daṇḍa-mukhya as "chiefs of the townsmen, country people and army"). sāmanta: neighbouring ruler or chief. In bheda-daṇḍābhyām daṇḍa is the upāya "force".
lines_deva: पुत्र.भ्रातृ.बन्धुषु साम.दानाभ्यां सिद्धिर् अनुरूपा, पौर.जानपद.दण्ड.मुख्येषु दान.भेदाभ्याम्, सामन्त.आटविकेषु भेद.दण्डाभ्याम्
lines_iast: putra.bhrātṛ.bandhuṣu sāma.dānābhyāṃ siddhir anurūpā, paura.jānapada.daṇḍa.mukhyeṣu dāna.bhedābhyām, sāmanta.āṭavikeṣu bheda.daṇḍābhyām

hindi: यह अनुलोम है; विपर्यय में प्रतिलोम।
english: This is in direct order; in the opposite [case], in inverse order.

hindi: मित्रों और अमित्रों में सिद्धि मिश्रित है।
english: Among allies and enemies, success is mixed.

hindi: क्योंकि उपाय परस्पर साधक हैं।
english: For the means are mutually accomplishing.

hindi: शत्रु के शंकित अमात्यों में प्रयुक्त साम शेष के प्रयोग को रोक देता है; दूष्य अमात्यों में दान, संघातों में भेद, शक्तिमानों में दण्ड।
english: Among the enemy’s suspected ministers, conciliation, when applied, turns back the use of the rest; among the treasonable ministers, gifts; among united groups, dissension; among the powerful, force.
notes: śaṅkita may mean "suspected" or "suspicious (of their own king)". sāntva = sāma, conciliation. saṅghāta: banded or united groups. Closing iti not rendered (unquoted).
lines_deva: शत्रोः शङ्कित.अमात्येषु सान्त्वं प्रयुक्तं शेष.प्रयोगं निवर्तयति, दूष्य.अमात्येषु दानम्, सङ्घातेषु भेदः, शक्तिमत्सु दण्ड इति
lines_iast: śatroḥ śaṅkita.amātyeṣu sāntvaṃ prayuktaṃ śeṣa.prayogaṃ nivartayati, dūṣya.amātyeṣu dānam, saṅghāteṣu bhedaḥ, śaktimatsu daṇḍa iti

words.gloss: from connection with heaviness and lightness

hindi: और आपत्तियों के गुरुत्व और लघुत्व के योग से नियोग, विकल्प और समुच्चय होते हैं।
english: And from the connection of the adversities with heaviness and lightness, there are niyoga (restriction), vikalpa (option) and samuccaya (combination).
notes: The three terms are defined in units 74 to 76. yoga here = connection. Review: alternative construction: āpadām with niyoga-vikalpa-samuccayāḥ ('of/for the adversities'), 'from the connection of heaviness and lightness'.

hindi: “इसी उपाय से, दूसरे से नहीं” — नियोग है।
english: “By this very means, not by another” — niyoga (restriction).

hindi: “इससे या दूसरे से” — विकल्प है।
english: “By this or by another” — vikalpa (option).

hindi: “इससे और दूसरे से” — समुच्चय है।
english: “By this and by another” — samuccaya (combination).

hindi: उनमें एक योग वाले चार और तीन योग वाले, दो योग वाले छह, चार योग वाला एक।
english: Of these, four are of one combination and [four] of three combinations, six of two combinations, one of four combinations.
notes: The number of the three-combination kind is not stated; catvāraḥ is taken to govern both (four plus four plus six plus one gives the fifteen of unit 78). The count is bracketed in English.
lines_deva: तेषाम् एक.योगाश् चत्वारस् त्रि.योगाश् च, द्वि.योगाः षट्, एकश् चतुर्.योगः
lines_iast: teṣām eka.yogāś catvāras tri.yogāś ca, dvi.yogāḥ ṣaṭ, ekaś catur.yogaḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार पन्द्रह उपाय।
english: Thus, fifteen means.

hindi: उतने प्रतिलोम हैं।
english: That many [are] the inverse ones.

hindi: उनमें एक उपाय से सिद्धि एक-सिद्धि है, दो से द्वि-सिद्धि, तीन से त्रि-सिद्धि, चार से चतुः-सिद्धि।
english: Of these, success by one means is single success; by two, double success; by three, triple success; by four, fourfold success.
lines_deva: तेषाम् एकेन-उपायेन सिद्धिर् एक.सिद्धिः, द्वाभ्यां द्वि.सिद्धिः, त्रिभिस् त्रि.सिद्धिः, चतुर्भिश् चतुः.सिद्धिर् इति
lines_iast: teṣām ekena-upāyena siddhir eka.siddhiḥ, dvābhyāṃ dvi.siddhiḥ, tribhis tri.siddhiḥ, caturbhiś catuḥ.siddhir iti

words.gloss: from having dharma as its root
from having desire as its fruit
linked with dharma, gain and desire

hindi: अर्थ धर्म के मूल वाला और काम के फल वाला है, इसलिए अर्थ की जो सिद्धि धर्म, अर्थ और काम से जुड़ी है, वह सब अर्थों की सिद्धि है। इस प्रकार सिद्धियाँ।
english: Because gain has dharma as its root and desire as its fruit, that success of gain which is linked with dharma, gain and desire is the success of all aims. Thus, the successes.

text_flags.why: visarga lost (plain h in the e-text); the word is the nominative plural siddhayaḥ

notes: The printed line contains the danda marks and the verse number 81 inside the line; they are kept as tokens. sarva-artha: "all aims" (artha as aim); "all gains" is the alternative. anubandha: attached, connected, or consequent.
lines_deva: धर्म.मूलत्वात् काम.फलत्वाच् च-अर्थस्य धर्म.अर्थ.काम.अनुबन्धा या-अर्थस्य सिद्धिः सा सर्व.अर्थ.सिद्धिः । ८१ । इति सिद्धयह्
lines_iast: dharma.mūlatvāt kāma.phalatvāc ca-arthasya dharma.artha.kāma.anubandhā yā-arthasya siddhiḥ sā sarva.artha.siddhiḥ | 81 | iti siddhayah

hindi: दैव से अग्नि, जल, रोग, महामारी, पलायन, अकाल, आसुरी सृष्टि — इस प्रकार आपत्तियाँ।
english: From the divine: fire, water, disease, pestilence, flight, famine, demonic creation — thus the adversities.
notes: udaka (water) may mean flood. pramāra literally "dying off" (pestilence or epidemic). vidrava = flight, rout or panic; "flight" kept literal. The Sanskrit has no verb after daivāt.
lines_deva: दैवाद् अग्निर् उदकं व्याधिः प्रमारो विद्रवो दुर्भिक्षम् आसुरी सृष्टिर् इत्य् आपदः
lines_iast: daivād agnir udakaṃ vyādhiḥ pramāro vidravo durbhikṣam āsurī sṛṣṭir ity āpadaḥ

words.gloss: from prostration before deities and brahmins

hindi: उनकी सिद्धि देवताओं और ब्राह्मणों को प्रणाम करने से होती है।
english: Of these, success is from prostration before deities and brahmins.

text_flags.why: likely typo: "rpaṇi-" is meaningless, praṇipāta (prostration) fits the sense and the metre-free prose

notes: tāsām refers to the adversities (āpadaḥ) of unit 82. The printed rpaṇipātataḥ is not a word; praṇipātataḥ is read (see text_flags).

hindi: अतिवृष्टि, अनावृष्टि, या जो आसुरी सृष्टि हो — उसमें आथर्वण कर्म और सिद्धों के आरम्भ सिद्धियाँ हैं।
english: Excessive rain, or drought, or whatever creation may be demonic: in that, Atharvan action and the undertakings of holy men [are] the successes.
notes: The Sanskrit has no verb in the second line; "[are]" is a bare copula. siddhayaḥ is taken as the predicate. siddha-ārambha could also be "undertakings begun by the accomplished" or "undertakings whose success is assured". Atharvan action: action pertaining to Atharvan (the Atharvaveda); nothing more is stated.
lines_deva: अतिवृष्टिर् अवृष्टिर् वा सृष्टिर् वा या-आसुरी भवेत्
तस्याम् आथर्वणं कर्म सिद्ध.आरम्भाश् च सिद्धयः
lines_iast: ativṛṣṭir avṛṣṭir vā sṛṣṭir vā yā-āsurī bhavet
tasyām ātharvaṇaṃ karma siddha.ārambhāś ca siddhayaḥ
